MSFT.headline: Trump floats a tax on overseas data centers, but there is no rule yet to model
paragraphs: Nothing material happened in the last day. The loudest new item is President Trump saying on Friday that US tech companies will face "a tremendous tax" if they build AI data centers in other countries (AP). AP reports he gave no details and said he had not yet told his own officials about the plan, and the AP article does not name Microsoft.

If it ever became a real rule it would touch capex and cost of revenue, and possibly Intelligent Cloud revenue growth, because Microsoft builds a large share of its Azure capacity outside the US. Today there is no rate, no legal mechanism and no date, so no assumption moves. In the same remarks he urged communities to accept data centers and ask developers for payments, which is friendly in tone to the FY28 one point permitting haircut for Texas and Wyoming but is words only.

The other headlines are older news resurfacing and change nothing. Microsoft and Intel announced a long-term deal on November 18 covering multi-year Xeon chip supply and Intel packaging for Azure's own chips, with no dollar value or term given, so it supports supply behind the capex plan without changing a number. Microsoft's claim that Copilot is cheaper than Claude and ChatGPT is a sales pitch from its Ignite conference based on a study Microsoft paid for (The Next Web, citing Bloomberg), with no price change, so Productivity revenue growth stays as it is.
watch: Any written follow-up to the overseas data center tax: an executive order, a Treasury or Commerce action, or a bill, and whether Microsoft comments
Microsoft's final incident report on the Outlook outage and any figure for customer credits
Whether Microsoft briefs the House China committee on the reported ByteDance talks, and December 10 for the Texas grid operator's final report
MSFT.note: Confirmed by the companies: the Intel and Microsoft agreement (joint release read on Intel's site) and the Copilot price pitch (made on stage by a Microsoft executive, read second hand). Reported only: Trump's tax remark is on the record through AP but has no policy behind it, and we could not open the CNBC version. A CNBC headline about a UK cloud competition probe is headline only, article not read, and looks like an old story.
